div.l: A twelf moneth and excuse him atte fulle
Ful pⁱriuyli ek a fynch couþe he pulle
And yf he fond owher a good felawe
He wolde techyn him to han noon awe
In swich caas of the Erchedekenes curs
But yf māmnes soule were in his purs
For in his purs punysshed he shuld be
Purs is þe Erchedeknes helle seide he
But wel y woot he lyhede right in dede
Of cursyng owht ech gilty man him drede
For curs wil slee ryȝt as a soilling sauith
And also war him of a significauith
In daunger hadde he at his owne gyse
The yonge gerles of þe diocise
And knew hir consaill and what was al hire rede
A garland had he sette vp on his hede
As grete as it were for an Ale stake
A bokeler hadde he made him of a kake
With him þer rode a gentill pardoner
Of Rouncyuale his frend ⁊and his comper
That streght was comyn fro þe court of Rome
Ful lowde he songe come hyder loue to me
This somynoᵘur bar to hym a styf burdoıı̄un
Was neủere trompe of half so gret a sown
This ꝑpardoner hadde her as yelow as wax
But smothe it heng as doth a strike of flax
Bi ounces henge his lokkes that he hadde
And ther wit he his shuldernes ouer spradde
But thynne it lay by culpoıı̄uns on ⁊and oon
But hode for Iolite werede he noon
For it was trussed vp in his walet
Hym thoughte he rood al of þe newe get
Discheuele saf his cappe he rood al bare
Swich glarynge eighen hadde he as an hare
A v̉ernycle hadde he sowid vppon his cappe
His walet bi forn hym in his lappe
Bret ful of ꝑpardon comen fro Rome al hote
A voys he hadde as smal as a goote
No berd ne hadde he ne neủer schuld haue
As smothe it was as it were late shaue
I trowe he were a geldyng or a mar
